title: docs(backend): GAMIFICATION.md documents an XP reward table that does not exist in the code

labels.name: backlog
labels.description: Tracked for future work; not blocking

body:
Split out of #12426, which surfaced this while auditing the XP award path. Found by @pacocartones — thank you.

`docs/frameworks/GAMIFICATION.md:239-252` documents an XP reward table that does not match `XP_REWARDS` in `src/lib/gamification/xp.ts:155-160`. The docs are not describing a version of the code that exists.

## Names that exist only in the docs

| Documented | Value | In `XP_REWARDS`? |
|---|---|---|
| `badge_earned` | 25 | ❌ — the code has `badge_unlock: 10` |
| `streak_milestone` | 15 | ❌ — the code has `streak_bonus: 2` |
| `referral` | — | ❌ no such action |
| `model_diversity` | — | ❌ no such action |
| `compression_use` | — | ❌ no such action |
| `skill_use` | — | ❌ no such action |

## Values that disagree

| Action | Docs | Code |
|---|---|---|
| `token_share` | 5 | 1 |
| `daily_login` | 3 | 5 |

## Decision needed before fixing

Which table is authoritative? Correcting the docs to match the code and raising the code's rewards to match the docs are both defensible, and the answer determines whether this is a docs-only change or lands together with #12426 (which tracks the fact that `streak_bonus` and `badge_unlock` are never paid at all — `getXpForAction` in `src/lib/gamification/events.ts:108-120` uses its own hardcoded table that stops at `daily_login`).

Per `AGENTS.md` → "Documentation accuracy", documentation must describe verified behavior. Right now this table would fail that gate.

Refs #12426

title: fix(docker): Trivy CRITICAL gate red — CVE-2025-68121 (Go stdlib 1.24.1) in the prebuilt tls-client 1.15.1 .so

labels.name: dependencies
labels.description: Pull requests that update a dependency file

labels.name: docker
labels.description: Pull requests that update docker code

body:
## What

`docker-publish` on `release/v3.8.51` is red since 2026-08-30 01:32Z (run [33279620488](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/actions/runs/33279620488)): the blocking **Trivy CRITICAL gate** now reports

| Library | Vulnerability | Installed | Fixed | Where |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Go `stdlib` | [CVE-2025-68121](https://avd.aquasec.com/nvd/cve-2025-68121) — `crypto/tls`: incorrect certificate validation during TLS session resumption | v1.24.1 | 1.24.13 / 1.25.7 | `app/node_modules/tls-client-node/bin/tls-client-linux-ubuntu-amd64-1.15.1.so` (gobinary) |

Nothing in the repo changed — the CVE entered Trivy's DB (the 08-29 18:43Z build on `main` skips the gate; the gate runs for every non-`main` image, so it also blocks the **`v3.8.51` tag build**).

## Why there is no bump

- The `.so` is fetched by `tls-client-node`'s postinstall from the **latest GitHub release of `bogdanfinn/tls-client`** — `v1.15.1` (2026-06-08) is still the latest and its `go.mod` declares `go 1.24.1`. No rebuilt upstream binary exists.
- `tls-client-node` npm: `0.2.0` is `latest` (2026-06-03); `1.0.4` is an older, different package lineage (April), not a fix.
- `ignore-unfixed: true` does not cover it because Go **has** a fixed stdlib version — only the upstream binary is not rebuilt.

## Remedy applied (per `docs/security/SUPPLY_CHAIN.md` → "CVE Variance", item 2)

`.trivyignore` entry for `CVE-2025-68121` with justification + this issue as tracker + expiry. Exposure note: the binary is only loaded by the web-provider executors that impersonate a browser TLS fingerprint (claude-web / grok-web / lmarena / perplexity-web / notion-web); handshakes go through `bogdanfinn/utls`, and the affected path is `crypto/tls` session resumption on the client side.

## To close this issue

Any of: a `bogdanfinn/tls-client` release built with Go ≥ 1.24.13 (then remove the `.trivyignore` line and verify the gate); or build the `.so` ourselves from `v1.15.1` sources with a patched Go toolchain and pin it via `TLS_CLIENT_VERSION` / a vendored asset. Revisit at the next base-image / dep bump and **before the `v3.8.51` tag**.

body:

body:
## Summary
Adopt **Obscura** (Rust, ~30MB RAM headless browser, Apache-2.0, CDP-compatible) as the primary browser engine for the browser-backed providers, with Playwright Chromium / desktop Chrome as the automatic fallback. Motivation: Chromium is memory-heavy (150-400+MB) and frequently fails (OOM / NSS lib crashes) on the Cloudflare Playground executor, and browser-grade TLS fingerprints are required by both Cloudflare Playground (WebSocket upgrade) and DuckDuckGo (VQD challenge, 418 ERR_BN_LIMIT IP bans).

## Why Obscura
- Only ~30MB RAM vs 150-400MB for Chromium — critical at scale.
- No system dependencies (no NSS/NSPR libs — fixes the Cloudflare crash permanently).
- CDP-compatible — existing Playwright code works via `chromium.connectOverCDP()` with minimal changes.
- Built-in proxy support (HTTP/SOCKS5 via `--proxy`) — enables IP rotation for DuckDuckGo.
- Stealth mode randomizes TLS/canvas fingerprints per session, passing Cloudflare checks.
- Apache-2.0 (Lightpanda is AGPL-3.0 — disqualified as viral).

## Validation Already Done
In a prior investigation session, Obscura was:
- Installed and confirmed to launch as a CDP server (Playwright connects).
- **Loaded Cloudflare Playground successfully** (title "AI Playground" with real content).
- **Opened the WebSocket to Cloudflare Playground (readyState 1 OPEN)** — Obscura's TLS fingerprint passes Cloudflare's checks.

## Current Architecture (what we're replacing)
- `open-sse/services/browserPool.ts` — shared stealth Chromium pool (DuckDuckGo VQD, Claude-web Turnstile). Prefers `cloakbrowser`, falls back to `playwright`.
- `open-sse/executors/cloudflare-playground.ts` — launches Playwright Chromium (or `CLOUDFLARE_PLAYGROUND_CHROME_PATH`), opens the model WebSocket inside the page context because only a real browser TLS stack passes.

## Desired Integration (Obscura-first, Chromium fallback)
1. **Add Obscura as a browser backend** that Playwright connects to via `chromium.connectOverCDP()` (Obscura runs as a CDP server on a local port).
2. **Order of preference**: Obscura → Playwright Chromium → `CLOUDFLARE_PLAYGROUND_CHROME_PATH` desktop Chrome.
3. If Obscura is unavailable or fails to launch, silently fall back to the existing Chromium/Chrome path (current behavior preserved).
4. **IP rotation**: wire DuckDuckGo (and optionally Cloudflare) through Obscura's `--proxy` (HTTP/SOCKS5), with Tor or a local rotating proxy chain as the rotation source, to mitigate `418 ERR_BN_LIMIT` IP bans.
5. Config-driven: env var to select engine / disable (e.g. `OMNIROUTE_BROWSER_ENGINE=obscura|playwright|chrome`) mirroring the existing `OMNIROUTE_BROWSER_POOL=off` switch.

## Failing Log Excerpt (Chromium crash on Cloudflare)
\`\`\`
cloudflare-playground executor:
browserType.launch: Target page, context or browser has been closed
(fixed this once with ~/lib/nss, but recurs and is memory-heavy)
\`\`\`

DuckDuckGo:
\`\`\`
ddgw/gpt-5.4-mini → 418 ERR_BN_LIMIT (IP ban, not cookie-fixable)
\`\`\`

## Scope / Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Obscura binary downloaded/installable; server finds it via PATH or config.
- [ ] Cloudflare Playground routes through Obscura first; falls back to Chromium/Chrome if Obscura fails.
- [ ] browserPool.ts can hand out Obscura-backed contexts; falls back for DDG/Claude-web.
- [ ] Proxy/IP-rotation hook for DDG; ban detection (418) routes to rotation.
- [ ] Zero behavior change when Obscura is absent (pure fallback).

## Related
- Issue #12273 (large-input routing collapse) — separate concern.
- Workspace: `opensource-elearning/omniroute-fixes`
- Obscura: https://github.com/h4ckf0r0day/obscura
